568	### Criterion 6: Conclusion-to-Ground-Truth Traceability
569	
570	Scores the relationship between the **Conclusion section** (section 6) claims and the
571	**Derivation Chains** (section 4) that produced them — a cross-section structural property
572	of the signed-off analysis as a whole. Quoted span: where the band is determined by whether a section-6 claim traces to a named section-4 chain, it must be drawn from the self-audit scan's claim-inventory table row or rows that determine the band, not from the Conclusion prose directly. Where the band is determined by the Key Insight being a restatement of the recommended approach rather than a non-obvious finding — a semantic property the claim-inventory table carries no column for — quote the analysis text directly.
573	
574	- **Rigorous** — every claim in the Conclusion section (recommended approach, key insight,
575	  trade-offs acknowledged) traces to a specific named derivation chain in section 4; the
576	  Conclusion section introduces no new claims that did not appear in section 4; the Key
577	  Insight names a non-obvious finding — a result that reasoning by analogy or convention
578	  does not reach — rather than restating the recommended approach.
579	
580	- **Sound** — most Conclusion claims trace to chains in section 4, but one claim is introduced
581	  for the first time in the Conclusion section (new reasoning not present in any derivation
582	  chain); OR the Key Insight is a restatement of the recommended approach rather than a
583	  non-obvious finding.
584	
585	- **Hand-wavy** — the Conclusion section contains claims that contradict or are inconsistent
586	  with the derivation chains in section 4; OR multiple new claims appear in the Conclusion
587	  section that are not present in any derivation chain.
588	
589	- **Absent** — the Conclusion section contains claims with no corresponding derivation chain
590	  anywhere in section 4; OR the Conclusion section is absent or empty; OR every item in the
591	  Conclusion is new reasoning not established by any derivation chain — the Conclusion section
592	  has been used to introduce the analysis's conclusions rather than to synthesize them.
593	
594	The extraction and caveat rules the bands above are scored against are stated here verbatim so the grading instrument carries them, not just the surface it grades.
595	
596	A Conclusion-section claim is a bold lead-in whose colon closes the bold span, or a numbered or bulleted list item, and the four lead-ins this template prescribes — `**Recommended approach:**`, `**Key insight:**`, `**Trade-offs acknowledged:**` and `**Confidence:**` — are always claims and each must cite a chain; the `**Confidence:**` line discharges that obligation through the chains D-07 already requires it to name, and a HIGH line whose justification prose names no chain is the one position where this rule and the extractor can disagree, so name the chain there too; nothing inside a fenced block is ever a claim whatever its shape, a near-paraphrase restatement or direct entailment of an already-cited claim earlier in the same section is not a second claim, and prose carrying neither a bold colon lead-in nor a list marker is not a claim at all. 597	
598	A caveat qualifying an existing Conclusion-section claim either names the chain it qualifies inline or carries the marker `no chain — flagged assumption only` (em dash, lower case, no trailing punctuation inside the marker), and a marked caveat still scores untraced: the marker discloses the gap, it does not discharge the claim, because it is honest labelling rather than a citation and the extractor is deliberately not taught to recognise it. 602	## Usage Note
603	
604	Score every criterion. Produce one verdict block per criterion, using the prescribed format
605	from the Verdict Block Format section above. The analysis must clear the gate (no criterion

607	presented. If either condition is not met, revise the relevant sections and re-score — bounded
608	to **at most one re-perception pass** per analysis, per the rule stated in full under "How to
609	Apply This Gate" at the top of this document. If a criterion still fails after that single
610	pass, present it as an unresolved gap with a stated confidence caveat instead of re-scoring
611	again. This closing note restates that bound; it does not create a second, looser one.

73:→ the real governing constraint on this agent's self-containment is not "every technique's full text must be inlined" — that would only be forced if `Read` itself were blocked — it is narrower: whatever text the agent needs *unconditionally at turn 0* to structure its first actions must be present without a tool call, and the eight companion-technique procedures are invoked contingently, phase-by-phase, exactly like the two appendices GT-10 already moved off this list
74:→ the line-count floor the actual constraint permits, computed by removing the trailer from the current body, is 1,378 − 520 = 858 lines, and production has already run leaner than even that: 807 lines at the v9.4.0 commit (GT-11) — so the "inline everything" treatment of the remaining five techniques is a convention carried over from the body's own history, not a requirement the tool restrictions impose
81:GT-10 (an identical split-style intervention — de-inlining two appendices — was already executed once, explicitly citing META-Q4) + GT-11 (the budget was exceeded again afterward, from entirely unrelated feature growth)
82:→ moving content out of the body once does not prevent new content from accreting back past any chosen threshold, because nothing in the current repository measures or gates that growth as it happens (GT-3)
83:→ a split justified only by the raw number recreates the same failure GT-10/GT-11 already demonstrate; a split is durably justified only when it removes content that is independently a defect — duplicate or dead content (GT-6, GT-7) — or is paired with a mechanism that keeps the file from drifting back up unmeasured
90:GT-6 (verbatim duplication) + GT-10 (proven precedent for the de-inline pattern) + GT-12 (a live measurement instrument already exists) + GT-2 (the requirement's own statement is unrecoverable)

93:→ recommend the composite: delete the 520-line Companion Techniques trailer and route all eight techniques through the Read-on-demand pattern already proven for two appendices and three techniques; formally re-record META-Q4 as a non-gating, visibility-only item with an honest current statement; and commission a live QUAL-01 run comparing the current and de-duplicated bodies before pursuing any further compression

101:→[2nd] maintainers gain a single-source-of-truth for every companion technique's procedure text, removing the dual-edit obligation between the reference files and the inlined trailer that this project's own audit record already mishandled once (GT-13); the agent itself trades 520 unconditionally-loaded lines for up to five additional conditional `Read` calls in a run that exercises every technique, versus the up-to-three it already issues today; whoever pays the API/context bill pays strictly less per invocation regardless of which techniques fire in a given run

In brief: the prompt's framing (878 lines, "enforced as a regression gate") describes a superseded repo state. I verified directly that the body is now **1,378 lines**, and META-Q4 is tiered `audit-only` with `rerun_by: "none"` and its own original requirement statement recorded as **"unrecoverable"** — nothing currently gates or even reports the line count. Rather than the reflexive split, the analysis found a specific, independently verified defect: a ~520-line block fully duplicates (byte-identical, confirmed by `diff`) all eight companion-technique procedures, and the body's own instructions then redundantly re-`Read` three of those eight via a tool call that fetches content already sitting in context. The recommendation (MEDIUM confidence) is a composite: remove that duplication via the Read-on-demand pattern already proven elsewhere in this codebase, formally re-record META-Q4 honestly instead of leaving it "unrecoverable," and commission the project's own existing QUAL-01 measurement harness to actually test whether size at this scale affects quality — rather than either blindly splitting or assuming (without evidence) that size doesn't matter.
